items.title: Here’s Why Dividend Kings Coca-Cola, Procter & Gamble, and Colgate-Palmolive Are Hitting 52-Week Highs Following Midterm Election Results

items.summary: PEP's snack pricing and affordability actions are fueling volume gains and stronger consumer demand, while rising costs and margin pressures remain challenging.

items.title: Walmart's Dec. 11 Dividend Isn't the Real Reason to Own the Stock
items.summary: Walmart won't offer much in terms of income, but its ability to boost dividend payouts for 53 consecutive years shows the strength of its business model.

items.title: Does Raised 2026 Guidance Change The Bull Case For Coca Cola Stock?
items.summary: Coca-Cola reported third quarter 2026 results with sales of US$13,380 million and net income of US$4,009 million, and raised full year earnings guidance alongside its 64th consecutive annual dividend increase. The combination of higher earnings per share, stronger free cash flow guidance and another dividend raise reinforces Coca-Cola's income focused appeal while highlighting continued demand for its broad beverage portfolio. items.title: Roth IRA vs. Taxable Account: How Much of $13,467 in Dividends Would You Keep?
items.summary: A $500,000 portfolio of six blue-chip dividend growers kicks off thousands in annual income, but where you hold those shares determines how much of that income you actually get to keep.

items.title: Inflation Is Running Above 3%. These 3 Dividend Stocks Have the Pricing Power to Keep Up.
items.summary: When inflation eats into your dividend's buying power, pricing power becomes the one trait separating stocks that keep up from those that quietly fall behind. Three consumer giants are charging more and still selling more, and the gap between them matters more than most investors realize.

items.title: Coca-Cola (KO) Weighs India Bottling IPO Through Hindustan Coca-Cola Holdings
items.summary: Coca-Cola (NYSE:KO) is reportedly weighing an IPO of its Indian bottling operations through Hindustan Coca-Cola Holdings. The potential listing would involve Coca-Cola's company owned bottling assets in India, a key market within its global network. Management is said to be in the early stages of assessing options, including structure and timing, with no final decision disclosed. The exploration of an IPO for Hindustan Coca-Cola should not be the only factor shaping your view on KO today...

items.title: Coca-Cola Pays Warren Buffett’s Berkshire $848 Million a Year as Jim Cramer Says Buy KO Stock
items.summary: Berkshire's $1.3 billion Coca-Cola bet now pays it $848 million a year, and with the stock near a record high, Jim Cramer says he'd still buy KO.
